question: Normal-mode vector metric and IR-column alignment audit. Use the bundled completed water Q-Chem source without inventing a new calculation. Read the three mode displacement tensors, three frequencies and three IR intensities in printed mode order. Flatten each mode in [atom0 x,y,z,atom1 x,y,z,atom2 x,y,z] order into M(3x9). Report frequencies,ir_intensities,plain_gram=M M^T, and weighted_gram=(M D)(M D)^T with D=diag(4,4,4,1,1,1,1,1,1). These explicitly declared metric weights use O:H=16:1 as a model convention. Report ascending spectra plain_spectrum,weighted_spectrum, and intensity_fractions = intensities/sum(intensities). Do not assume printed rounded displacement vectors are orthonormal in either metric. Return the named answer fields as JSON. Numeric values must agree within absolute 1e-6 plus relative 1e-6; winner ties use absolute 1e-9. Array order follows the supplied data order unless explicitly stated otherwise. Required output fields: plain_gram, plain_spectrum, weighted_gram, weighted_spectrum, frequencies, ir_intensities, intensity_fractions. The bundled source is reused as a fixed computational record; this exercise does not run quantum chemistry or assign a Materials Project identity.

contract.description: Compute ascending real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors after a near-symmetry check. The lower triangle defines the symmetric matrix; signs and repeated-subspace bases are arbitrary.

eigenvectors.description: Complete n-by-n orthonormal eigenvector matrix;column j belongs to eigenvalues[j]. Signs are arbitrary. Repeated-eigenvalue bases may rotate within the eigenspace. The symmetric source matrix is defined by its lower triangle.

limitations: Float64 real symmetric decomposition only;near-symmetry is checked before lower-triangle interpretation.
Signs and degenerate eigenspace bases are not stable scientific identifiers;compare eigen-equations or projectors.
No sorting by a physical label,normal-mode interpretation or model covariance assumption is inferred.
